paper.title: SLTUNET: A Simple Unified Model for Sign Language Translation
paper.citation: Biao Zhang, Mathias Müller, and Rico Sennrich. SLTUNET: A Simple Unified Model for Sign Language Translation. In The Eleventh International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR), 2023.

sources.role: Target and protocol source. The assignment pointed at the OpenReview PDF, but openreview.net served an HTTP 403 bot challenge to both the fetch tool and curl on 2026-09-13, so the arXiv v1 copy of the same ICLR 2023 camera-ready was hashed instead. The arXiv copy carries the 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2023' header and the same tables; the OpenReview record remains the canonical citation.

The authors' official implementation, linked from the paper abstract. Contains the SLTUNET model, the adapted SMKD sign-embedding pretraining code under smkd/, the evaluation metrics under eval/, the PHOENIX walk-through under example/, and the DGS3-T construction scripts under dgs3-t/. Master branch, latest commit dated 2023-07-10.

Authors' released trained models for PHOENIX and CSL-Daily (phoenix.tar.gz, csldaily.tar.gz, csldaily2.tar.gz, dgs3-t.tar.gz), announced in the repository README on 2023-07-09. Directory listing confirmed reachable on 2026-09-13 but no archive has been downloaded or hashed yet, so this source is not pinned. Intended use is an evaluation-path preflight and a check of the decoding/metric pipeline before any training run; a score obtained from the authors' own weights verifies the artifact and is not by itself a reproduction of their training.

Upstream SMKD/VAC_CSLR implementation cited by the paper (footnote 1) as the sign embedding extractor. The sltunet repository vendors an adapted copy under smkd/, so the vendored copy pinned through published-code is the artifact that will actually run; this upstream is recorded because the paper cites it and because the paper reports retraining SMKD with a 2D ResNet34 backbone.

status.numerical_agreement_basis: No target has produced a value: no environment has been built and no run has been executed, so there is nothing comparable to assess.
status.preference_level_basis: The authors published a complete implementation at a pinnable commit, including training, decoding, and metric code, so the attempt starts at preference level 1. The level has not yet been tested by execution; the TensorFlow 1.15 / Python 3.8 requirement is expected to force container work and may force level 2 patches.

experiments.system: SLTUNET, final configuration (system 15 of Table 2): d=256, h=4, dff=4096, N^P_enc=1, N^S_enc=5, N_dec=6, CTC alpha=0.3, stochastic BPE dropout (rate 0.2, stochastic rate 0.6), Xavier gain 0.5, sign-frame random crop and horizontal flip, trained on the Equation 4 multi-task objective with MT data, using sign embeddings from the retrained SMKD model with a 2D ResNet34 backbone. Evaluated end-to-end (Sign2Text).
experiments.checkpoint_rule: Average of the best 10 checkpoints ranked by dev-set Sign2Text performance, then beam search with beam size 8 and a length penalty tuned on the dev set (paper Appendix A.1; repository checkpoint_averaging.py and example/test.sh).

environment_plan.published_requirements: python==3.8, tensorflow==1.15 (repository README 'Requirement'); no requirements.txt or lockfile is published.
environment_plan.base_image_conflict: The repository's standard GPU base image ghcr.io/sign-language-processing/reproduction:latest supplies NVIDIA NGC PyTorch. SLTUNET is TensorFlow 1.15, which needs CUDA 10.0 / cuDNN 7.x and will not run on that image, so a paper-specific Dockerfile is expected. This is an environment adaptation, not a change to the published code, and the exact image has not been chosen or built yet.
environment_plan.video_decoding: The published SLTUNET training path consumes precomputed SMKD sign features in .h5 files rather than decoding video, so no video decoder is introduced for it. The upstream SMKD feature-extraction step does read frames and is where simple-video-utils would apply if that step is rerun.
environment_plan.planned_first_check: An evaluation-path preflight using the authors' released PHOENIX checkpoint, to exercise decoding, checkpoint averaging, and eval/metrics.py against the published Table 4 numbers before committing to SMKD pretraining plus full SLTUNET training.

open_questions: Whether the study wants the DGS3-T targets pursued at all, given that permission from the University of Hamburg is a prerequisite and may not be obtainable within the study.
